reason: While the text depicts hierarchical structures (nobles, officials, governor, common people), it does not emphasize or encourage hierarchy as a positive principle. Rather, it critiques and actively works against hierarchical exploitation. Nehemiah, though in a position of authority, confronts the nobles and officials for their oppression of the people ('You exact usury from your own brethren'). He uses his authority to enforce equitable treatment and the release of those enslaved due to debt—actions that deliberately undermine exploitative hierarchical practices. The passage emphasizes mutual human solidarity and just treatment rather than the reinforcement of hierarchical authority.
